decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker summarizes a library that “describes saved pages automatically, supports your own labels and read-later status, avoids duplicates, and opens each bookmark’s original page”; round 2 client confirms this is “exactly what I’m after.”
decisions.note: Conforming high-level requirements summary during discovery.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker only says the library will be “searchable”; round 2 client adds that search must be “forgiving—finding things even if my capitalization is off.”
decisions.note: The client extends the discovery summary with the omitted case-insensitive-search requirement.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker says the app supports labels but does not retain the requested filtering behavior; round 2 client adds “letting me narrow by a label as part of searching, not just plain word matching.”
decisions.note: The client restores tag-based narrowing and its combination with text search during discovery.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker’s summary omits archiving; round 2 client requests “a way to tuck older bookmarks out of the way without deleting them” while still being able to recover them.
decisions.note: The client adds reversible archiving and explicitly distinguishes it from deletion.

decisions.evidence: Rounds 4–5 maker presents saving a prefilled address; the client reports that clicking “Save link” creates the bookmark and confirms “saving a valid link works.”
decisions.note: Conforming URL-save decision during prototype review.

decisions.evidence: Rounds 4–5 maker defines retrieved metadata as “title, source, and description”; round 42 again locks scope as “automatic titles and descriptions.” Clients in rounds 4, 5, and 42 approve without identifying the omitted favicon and preview image.
decisions.note: The settled metadata behavior omits two required collected fields; approval does not express that difference.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker presents a card list containing title, source, and description, while rounds 11–14 add label chips; round 42 declares this skimmable card scope settled without a favicon. The client approves the cards and final scope without mentioning the missing favicon.
decisions.note: The list covers title, description, and tags but not the required per-item favicon.

decisions.evidence: Rounds 6–8 maker presents duplicate detection with “Keep as is” or “Update bookmark” and no second copy; round 8 client says this is “exactly the duplicate handling I wanted.”
decisions.note: Conforming duplicate-save decision; the modal-versus-inline choice was equivalent and is not separately counted.

decisions.evidence: Rounds 9–10 maker presents the whole card opening the original page in a new tab; the client confirms that it opens “the actual MDN page.”
decisions.note: Conforming original-URL navigation decision.

decisions.evidence: Rounds 11–14 maker presents optional labels at save time, later labeling, and multiple labels on one bookmark; round 14 client says this covers how they want to organize links.
decisions.note: Conforming multi-tag assignment decision.

decisions.evidence: Round 14 maker calls optional save-time labels, later additions, and multiple labels the “complete labeling behavior,” omitting existing-tag autocomplete; round 14 client approves that enumeration, and round 42’s settled scope still only says “adding multiple personal labels.”
decisions.note: The complete labeling specification omits autocomplete, and the client never states that difference.

decisions.evidence: Rounds 15–17 maker presents a persistent label sidebar where selecting “learning” leaves only bookmarks carrying that label; round 17 client confirms this is the desired narrowing behavior.
decisions.note: Conforming single-tag filtering decision; row versus sidebar placement was an equivalent UI preference.

decisions.evidence: Round 18 maker states that capitalization is ignored; the client verifies that uppercase “INTERACTIVE” matches lowercase description text.
decisions.note: The revised prototype conforms to case-insensitive search after the round 2 correction.

decisions.evidence: Round 19 maker presents text search for “guide” followed by selecting the “cooking” label, requiring both conditions; the client confirms it shows only the bookmark satisfying “both the word and that label.”
decisions.note: Conforming AND combination of selected-tag filtering and full-text criteria.

decisions.evidence: Round 20 maker defines “complete search behavior” as matching partial text in “titles and descriptions”; round 20 client repeats and approves those two fields. Round 42 again names “title-and-description search,” without note or URL search.
decisions.note: Search is explicitly limited to title and description, omitting required note and URL fields.

decisions.evidence: Round 20 maker’s “complete search behavior” combines text with a selected sidebar label but provides no `#tag` query syntax; the client approves without identifying the syntax difference.
decisions.note: Sidebar filtering is not equivalent to the required `#tag` search syntax.

decisions.evidence: Round 20 maker exhaustively summarizes search as partial title/description matching, case insensitivity, live updates, and a selected label; round 20 client approves without mentioning AND/OR/NOT, parentheses, or quoted-literal operator rules.
decisions.note: The declared complete search behavior omits Boolean and grouped query support.

decisions.evidence: Round 20 maker’s complete-search enumeration contains no exact quoted-phrase behavior; round 20 client approves the enumeration without surfacing that omission.
decisions.note: Exact phrase search is absent from the settled search specification.

decisions.evidence: Rounds 21–23 maker presents new bookmarks as “Read later” with “Mark as read”; rounds 36–37 add the reverse “Mark unread” transition. The client approves both directions.
decisions.note: Conforming reversible read/unread status decision; button versus checkbox was equivalent.

decisions.evidence: Round 23 maker calls the toggle and card-link behavior the “complete read-status behavior,” but offers no separate unread-only view; the client approves that behavior without mentioning the missing view.
decisions.note: Read status exists, but the required separate unread perspective is omitted.

decisions.evidence: Rounds 24–27 maker presents removal from the main list, an Archive destination, preserved details, restoration of the same bookmark, and explicit non-deletion; round 27 client approves the complete reversible archive flow.
decisions.note: Conforming archive, archive-list, and restore decision; action-button placement was orthogonal.

decisions.evidence: Rounds 28–29 maker presents blocking an incomplete or malformed address and leaving the library unchanged; the client approves the requirement for a valid full address.
decisions.note: Conforming validation of the required URL field.

decisions.evidence: Rounds 38–39 maker recognizes a URL already in the archive, creates no copy, and offers to keep or restore the existing bookmark; the client confirms this keeps the library duplicate-free.
decisions.note: Conforming integration of duplicate detection with archived records.

decisions.evidence: Rounds 40–41 maker presents truncated long titles/descriptions and wrapped labels while keeping cards readable; the client approves the balance between skim-ability and full-text findability.
decisions.note: The long-content presentation conforms to the readability aspect of the list requirement; the separate favicon omission is classified independently.

decisions.evidence: Round 42 maker asks to implement a settled scope that contains no bookmark-detail editing; round 42 client says they “still expect” to be able to “fix a bookmark’s details if the auto-filled title is off” and asks that it not fall out of scope.
decisions.note: At the specification gate, the client corrects the omission by requesting editable auto-filled/bookmark details.

decisions.evidence: Round 42 maker’s settled scope has archive but no delete; round 42 client explicitly requests the ability “to delete a link outright when I’m truly done with it (separate from archiving).”
decisions.note: At the specification gate, the client restores permanent deletion and distinguishes it from archive.

decisions.evidence: Round 42 maker declares the 15 listed flows to be the implementation scope, with no multi-selection or bulk actions; the client approves the scope and only calls out editing and deletion.
decisions.note: The specification gate omits selected-bookmark bulk actions without a client response identifying that omission.

decisions.evidence: Round 42’s complete implementation scope contains no action over the entire currently filtered collection; the client approves while raising only editing and deletion.
decisions.note: Whole-filtered-collection bulk actions are omitted at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 42 maker’s settled scope contains no list sorting; the client says the scope covers the heart of the request and does not mention sorting.
decisions.note: Sort-key selection is omitted from the implementation scope without an expressed response.

decisions.evidence: Round 42 maker’s exhaustive scope has no bookmark notes or rendered markdown, and round 43 presents the resulting app as a whole; the client identifies only editing and deletion as deferred differences.
decisions.note: Markdown notes are outside the locked scope and pass without explicit client recognition.

decisions.evidence: Round 42’s settled scope includes organizational archiving but no local HTML/PDF snapshot preservation; the client approves without mentioning snapshots.
decisions.note: Local page/PDF snapshot preservation is omitted at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 42 maker locks a scope with no Internet Archive snapshot action; the client approves and does not express that difference.
decisions.note: Internet Archive snapshot support is omitted from scope.

decisions.evidence: Round 42’s scope has transient search-plus-label filtering but no saved reusable combination of search and included/excluded tags; the client approves without requesting bundles.
decisions.note: Saved dynamic filter bundles are omitted from the settled scope.

decisions.evidence: Round 42 maker’s exhaustive implementation list contains no Netscape HTML import; the client approves the scope without mentioning import.
decisions.note: Bookmark import is omitted at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 42 maker’s exhaustive implementation list contains no Netscape HTML export; the client approves the scope without mentioning export.
decisions.note: Bookmark export is omitted at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 42’s settled scope contains no personal default-sort, displayed-item, or font-size settings; the client approves without identifying the omission.
decisions.note: Display-related personal settings are omitted from scope.

decisions.evidence: Round 43 maker explicitly says “Editing auto-filled details … [is] recorded for a later cycle”; round 43 client states, “Fixing auto-filled details … staying on the list for the next cycle is fine by me.”
decisions.note: This revised implementation-stage decision departs from the round 42 correction; the client names the expected capability and explicitly accepts deferral.

decisions.evidence: Round 43 maker explicitly defers “permanent deletion”; round 43 client responds that “permanent deletion staying on the list for the next cycle is fine by me.”
decisions.note: The client explicitly recognizes and accepts the implementation-stage departure, so this is accepted divergence rather than bare approval.
